pois.name: Wako Building
pois.description: Ginza's defining symbol — the 1932 neoclassical building with its famous clock tower at the corner of Chuo-dori and Harumi-dori. Its basement jewellery and watchmaking counters are the finest in Japan. The clock bell chimes every hour across the intersection.

pois.name: GINZA SIX
pois.description: Ginza's largest luxury flagship — 13 floors, 240+ boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Céline, Dior, Hermès), restaurants, and a rooftop garden. The 6-storey atrium houses a 30-metre mobile by Jeff Koons. Japan's biggest luxury department store.

pois.name: Kabuki-za Theatre
pois.description: Tokyo's home of traditional kabuki — the fifth building on this site (2013) in neo-Momoyama style with ornate green roof curves. Single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) let casual visitors experience Japan's most theatrical performance tradition.

pois.name: Ginza Shopping Street
pois.description: The central boulevard of Ginza, closed to traffic every weekend afternoon as a 'pedestrian paradise'. Lined with Hermès (Renzo Piano), Cartier, Apple Ginza, Uniqlo and Mikimoto. The fashion axis of Tokyo since the Meiji era.

pois.name: Mitsukoshi Ginza
pois.description: The Ginza outpost of Japan's oldest department store chain (founded 1673) — 12 floors of fashion, food, and traditional crafts. The basement food hall (depachika) is considered Tokyo's finest, with Mitsukoshi-branded confections shipped nationally.
